lawyer:
Mr. Sk. Md. Mr. Abdul Quayum with Morshed ------ For the petitioner. 
Mr. Md. Omar Faruque ------ For the opposite parties.
parties:
Mosammat Rehana Akhter
Vs.
Rizia Begum and others
full_judgment:
The preemptor opposite party No. 1 filed Preemption Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 2002 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Mirsarai Sadar, Chittagong, under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for preemption of the case land, stating, in short that the total land under B.S. khatian No. 1196 belonged to Jabeda Khatun, Md. Yeasin, Foyez Ahmad and Aslam Miah; the said Jobeda Khatun sold out her portion to Fakir Ahmad that said Yeasin died leaving behind a wife, sons, namely, Shabuddin, Ruhul Amin, Md. Azim Uddin, Md. Tajul Islam and Zafor Ahmad; that said Ruhul Amin, Md. Azim Uddin, Zafor Ahmad and wife of Yeasin and her daughter sold out their portion to opposite party No. 4, Sudhir Chandra Sharma; that the said Foyez Amed died leaving behind the opposite parties Nos. 5 to 10 and the preemptor Rizia Begum; that said Aslam Miah gifted his portion to opposite parties Nos. 13 to 15; that the seller Fakir Ahmed had no other land in the khatian after the sale in question and as such he was not made a party to the case; that the seller without any notice to the preemptor sold out the land in question to the preemptee-opposite party-petitioner and the preemptor came to know the same on 24.01.2002; that the preemptor is a co-sharer by inheritance in the khatian and the preemptee is a stranger to the khatian in question and as such she is entitled to get the land in question by preemption. 

 3. The Preemption Miscellaneous Case was contested by the preemptee-opposite party-petitioner by filling written Objection denying the averments made in the Miscellaneous petition and stating, in short that the Preemption Miscellaneous case is not maintainable in its form and manner and is liable to be rejected for defect of parties; that the Preemption Miscellaneous Case is barred by limitation; that the preemptor is not entitled to get the preemption and the case is liable to be dismissed on the ground of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence; that total 113 decimals land belonged to Jogendra Nath Roy Chowdhury and Abdul Majid in equal share but during R.S. survey operation Dag No. 528 of R.S. Khatian No. 514 was recorded in the name of Jogendra Nath Roy Chowdhury. Thereafter he sold out the same to Abdul Samad; that during B.S. survey operation the said land was recorded in B.S. khatian No. 1196 under B.S. dag Nos. 954,958 and 955/956/957. Land covered by B.S. dag No. 954 is 32 decimals and B.S. dag No. 958 covered 18 decimals; that thereafter the P.S. and B.S. recorded tenant Jobeda Khatun on 23.11.1981 sold out the case land to Fakir Ahmed; that thereafter said Fakir Ahmed being in need of money urgently requested the preemptor to purchase the land in question but she refused to purchase the same and thereafter the said Fakir Ahmed sold out the same to the preemptee-opposite party-petitioner on 10.12.2000 and she after her purchase has been possessing the same; that the preemptor is not a co-share in B.S. khatian No. 1196 as because the predecessor of the preemptor Foyez Ahmed never purchased land under R.S. dag No. 528 and she will not be able to prove the same. But the name of Foyez Ahmed was wrongly recorded in B.S. khatian No. 1196; that the P.S. and B.S. recorded tenant Jobeda Khatun sold out 12 decimals land on 23.11.1981 to Kabir Ahmed but the preemptor never claimed that and while the said Fakir Ahmed sold out the same to the preemptee-opposite party, then she claimed to purchase the land by preemption without having any right to get the same; that the seller before the sale in question requested the preemptor to purchase the- land in question but while she refused to purchase the same then the seller on his urgent necessity of money sold out the same to the preemptee-opposite party-petitioner; that in the aforesaid facts and circumstances the Preemption Case is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the learned trial Court having considered the evidence and materials on record, held that the case is barred by limitation and accordingly dismissed the preemption case, but the learned appellate Court though found that the case has been filed within time from date of completion of registration under Section 67 of the Registration Act, but the learned appellate Court committed error in allowing the appeal without considering the case of the pre-emptee that the preemptor is not a co-sharer in the disputed khatian which has been wrongly recorded in the name of his predecessor Foiz Ahmed who has no right title and interest in the case khatian. 

 9. Mr. Md. Omar Faruque, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties on the other hand submitted that the learned appellate Court on consideration of the evidence and materials on record rightly held that in a preemption proceeding the correctness of the disputed khatian cannot be inquired into and as such rightly held that the preemptor is a co-sharer in the case khatian and rightly allowed the appeal and thereby allowing the preemption case. 

 10. On perusal of the judgment and order passed by the learned trial Court, it appears, the learned trial Court held that the preemptor is a co-sharer in the B.S khatian; that the preemptor had knowledge about the disputed sale from the very beginning and she filed the case after 13 months of her knowledge about the disputed transfer; that though the preemptee challenged the correctness of B.S khatian No. 1196, but correctness of such khatian cannot be decided in a preemption case. With these findings the learned trial Court dismissed the preemption case. 

 11. On appeal, the learned appellate Court also held that in a preemption proceeding the correctness of the B.S khatian cannot be looked into and that only a civil Court can decide the correctness of a khatian; that as the B.S khatian has been recorded in the name of Foiz Ahmed the predecessor in interest of the preemptor, so the preemptor is a co-sharer; that the registration of the disputed kabala having been completed on 05.11.2002and the case having been filed on 26.01.2002, the case is not barred by limitation. With these findings the learned appellate Court allowed the preemption case. 

 12. Now the main question is whether in preemption proceeding the Court can consider the correctness of the disputed khatian in order to see whether the preemptors or his predecessor's name has been correctly recorded in the disputed khatian. It appears the preemptee in his written objection specifically stated that the disputed khatian published in the name of Foiz Ahmed predecessor of the preemptor was wrong in as much as Foiz Ahmed had no subsisting interest in the land of the khatian while the said khatian was recorded in his name. To substantiate this fact the preemptee specifically stated this fact in her written objection as well as in the deposition of O.P.W.1 her husband Nazrul Islam. The preemptee also cross-examined the P.W.1 preemptor on this point that the disputed khatian was wrongly printed in the name of Foiz Ahmed having no subsisting interest in the land of the khatian. It appears both the Courts held that in a pre-emption proceedings this kind of complicated question cannot be decided which can only be decided in a properly constituted civil suit. Mr. Abdul Quayum in support of his submission that in a preemption proceeding this kind of question about correctness of the khatian and correctness of the mutation proceeding and other similar maters can be considered has referred to the decision in the case of Kutu Chand Miah-Vs-Rabindra Kumar Deb and others reported in 22 DLR 29 and the decision of Md. Khairullah Bhuiyan-Vs- Haji Nurul Alam Chowdhury, being dead his heirs Amena Khatun and others reported in 35 DLR (AD) 338. On perusal of the 1st decision which has been reported in 22 DLR 294 it appears in the said decision it has been held that in a proceeding under Section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the correctness of the record of right can be inquired into and held that the recording of the applicants name in the record of right was not correct and accordingly the trial Court rejected the application for preemption, which was upheld by the High Court. Similarly in the 2nd decision reported in 35 DLR 338 it has been held that the order of Revenue Officer splitting up a joint-tenancy in whichever way it may be designed, if it severs the old relationship of the co-sharers and thereby destroys a co-sharer's statutory right of preemption, cannot be examined by the Court in a preemption proceeding in order to be satisfied that prima-facie the order was passed in accordance with law, that is to say, whether the mandatory provisions of section 117(e) of the E.B.S.A. and Tenancy Act were complied with on the face of the record. In the said decision it was further held:- "The scope of this examination cannot be so limited as to ask the Court to keep its eyes closed and to accept without hesitation whatever order is placed before it, simply because the order was passed by a competent Revenue Officer." 

 13. From the aforesaid decisions it can be said that in a pre-emption proceeding the Court can consider the correctness of the disputed khatian, but in the present case, it appears, both the Courts below held that the correctness of the disputed khatian cannot be considered in a preemption proceeding and accordingly, in my opinion, both the Courts below committed error in law in holding that correctness of the disputed khatian cannot be considered in the present proceeding and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the learned appellate Court are liable to be set aside and the case should be sent on remand to the learned appellate Court for fresh disposal.
